concerns.concern: The dμ/dn extraction divides by a quantity that can become small or change sign. This can create spurious peaks or divergences in the extracted compressibility.
concerns.quote: Eq. (7) has a denominator ρ(μ + eV_b) − ρ(μ), which can become small or change sign. This can produce spurious peaks or divergences.

concerns.concern: The extraction is done at a single probe bias (±42 mV). The authors never show that dμ/dn is independent of bias, which a genuine thermodynamic quantity must be.
concerns.quote: A thermodynamic dμ/dn must be independent of V_b. No test of this is shown.

concerns.concern: The phenomenological exponential transmission background is divided out before differentiation. Errors in its exponent or any residual filling dependence of the barrier therefore feed into dμ/dn, μ(n) and S(n). The exponent's uncertainty, fit range and temperature dependence are not reported.
concerns.quote: Any error in the exponent, or any residual filling dependence of the barrier, therefore adds a smooth error to dμ/dn.

concerns.concern: No full error propagation through the extraction equations is given. The background-fitting procedure is also not stated in the main text.
concerns.quote: state the background-fitting procedure in the main text and give full error propagation through Eqs. (3)/(7).

concerns.concern: The extracted entropy decreases with temperature in several intervals, which would imply negative specific heat and must be an artifact. These decreases are as large as the claimed plateaus and actually define the '20 K plateau'.
concerns.quote: Because (∂S/∂T)_ν = C/T ≥ 0, these segments imply negative specific heat and must be artifacts. They have the same magnitude as the "plateaus"

concerns.concern: Some entropies in Fig. 4b have error bars that extend below zero, which is unphysical.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b also contains entropies whose error bars extend below zero.

concerns.concern: The plateaus come from a three-point numerical derivative on a sparse temperature grid. This amplifies noise and drift, so the plateaus may be artifacts of the differentiation.
concerns.quote: a three-point numerical derivative of ∫μ dν over a sparse temperature grid (roughly 2–4 K steps), which amplifies noise and drift.

concerns.concern: The entropy error bars appear to omit systematic contributions. These include thermometry lag, temperature dependence of the transmission and the phonon channel, and the capacitance correction.
concerns.quote: The error bars do not appear to include systematic contributions

concerns.concern: The number of independent datasets behind the entropy results is not stated.
concerns.quote: The number of independent datasets is also not stated.

concerns.concern: μ is fixed to zero at the charge neutrality point at all temperatures, although μ_CNP(T) is unknown and generically temperature-dependent. A small drift would add spurious filling-linear entropy of several k_B, as large as the plateaus.
concerns.quote: A drift of only ~0.1 meV/K gives errors of several k_B per moiré cell.

concerns.concern: The entropy integration starts at ν = 4, so errors accumulate toward lower fillings.
concerns.quote: Integration starts at ν = 4, so errors accumulate toward lower fillings.

concerns.concern: S(ν = 4) = 0 is assumed up to 36–40 K. At those temperatures, thermal population of remote bands and the c-electron continuum may not be negligible.
concerns.quote: S(ν = 4) = 0 is assumed up to 36–40 K. At k_BT ≈ 3 meV, thermal population of the remote bands and the c-electron continuum is not obviously negligible

concerns.concern: Any temperature dependence of the quantum-capacitance filling correction or of the transmission normalization would also appear as spurious entropy.
concerns.quote: Any temperature dependence of the quantum-capacitance filling correction or of the T(n) normalization enters as spurious entropy in the same way.

concerns.concern: The authors claim local-moment entropy but show no in-plane-field test. Without one, the plateaus cannot be distinguished from other sources of temperature-dependent μ, such as band renormalization, thermal smearing across strain-split bands, or phonon excitations.
concerns.quote: Without this test, the plateaus cannot be distinguished from other sources of temperature-dependent μ

concerns.concern: The degeneracy comparison uses only a few integer points and only the electron side. The full ν ∈ [−4, 4] test of the 8-fold counting is never performed.
concerns.quote: The comparison is made only at a few integer points connected by lines, and only on the electron side.

concerns.concern: At 10 K the data lie notably below the predicted ln 4 and ln 6 values at several fillings. The claimed alignment therefore needs a quantitative fit with uncertainties.
concerns.quote: At 10 K the data (S ≈ 1–1.5 k_B at ν = 1–3) lie notably below ln 4 and ln 6 at several fillings

concerns.concern: The counting assumes fully random local moments and omits c-electron entropy, phonon entropy and inter-site correlations. The c-electron sector alone contributes appreciable entropy at 20 K.
concerns.quote: The counting assumes fully random local moments with no c-electron entropy, no phonon contribution and no inter-site correlations.

concerns.concern: The 4-fold and 8-fold models use different reference fillings (CNP versus ν = −4), with no microscopic justification for referencing the 4-fold manifold to the CNP.
concerns.quote: There is no microscopic justification for referencing the low-temperature 4-fold manifold to the CNP.

concerns.concern: The vanishing CNP entropy below 12 K is essentially guaranteed by the CNP gap and the chosen reference, so it is not independent support.
concerns.quote: is essentially guaranteed by the CNP gap and the chosen reference, so it is not independent support.

concerns.concern: The degeneracy counting formulas are written incorrectly. They should be binomial coefficients.
concerns.quote: should be binomial coefficients: k_B ln C(4,|ν|) and k_B ln C(8,ν+4).

concerns.concern: The tunneling model ignores the phonon-assisted inelastic process the device relies on. The measured signal is then a convolution involving phonon dispersion, Bose occupation (relevant to the temperature series) and matrix elements, not the simple DOS assumed.
concerns.quote: The measured signal is then not ρ(E_F + eV_b) as Eqs. (1)–(3) assume.

concerns.concern: Momentum-selective, orbital-dependent matrix elements may weight f and c electrons differently and in a filling-dependent way. An apparent heavy/light asymmetry could therefore partly be a matrix-element effect.
concerns.quote: an apparent heavy/light asymmetry could partly reflect orbital-selective matrix elements.

concerns.concern: Identifying E_F with μ(n) at about ±22 mV conflates the inelastic phonon threshold with the sample chemical potential.
concerns.quote: The identification "E_F = μ(n) ≈ ±22 mV" also conflates the inelastic threshold with the sample chemical potential.

concerns.concern: The heavy-below/light-above asymmetry is also produced by the established cascade/Hartree–Fock picture and was reported before. Since the manuscript admits the data fit both symmetric and symmetry-broken phases, claiming it 'verifies' the THF f/c picture is overstated.
concerns.quote: The claim that the asymmetry "verifies" heavy f- and light c-electrons is therefore overstated.

concerns.concern: The weaker hole-side asymmetry is neither analyzed nor reconciled with THF predictions for negative fillings.
concerns.quote: The weaker hole-side asymmetry is also not analyzed or reconciled with THF predictions for negative fillings.

concerns.concern: The 'cyclotron effective mass' from Eq. (4) turns an interaction-dominated compressibility into a non-interacting DOS mass. dμ/dn contains large Hartree and exchange contributions, so this is not a quasiparticle mass.
concerns.quote: In MATBG, dμ/dn contains large Hartree and exchange contributions.

concerns.concern: The heavy-mass regions sit where dμ/dn is near zero or negative, where Eq. (4) diverges or is undefined. It is unclear how these points are treated on the log-scale plots.
concerns.quote: There, Eq. (4) diverges or is undefined, and small offsets dominate. It is unclear how these points are treated on the log scales

concerns.concern: Fixing the degeneracy factor g′ = 4 contradicts the flavor-reset picture used elsewhere in the paper. Correcting it changes m* by factors of 2–4, comparable to the claimed tenfold renormalization.
concerns.quote: Correcting g′ changes m* by factors of 2–4, comparable to the claimed factor of 10.

concerns.concern: The light mass (~0.06 m_e) is lighter than flat-band estimates and comparable to the remote-band mass, suggesting interaction- or gap-induced contributions rather than c-band dispersion. Its comparison with bilayer graphene is not tied to a THF c-electron velocity.
concerns.quote: This suggests interaction- or gap-induced contributions rather than c-band dispersion.

concerns.concern: A numerical check suggests the plotted mass minima may not be consistent with g′ = 4.
concerns.quote: It is unclear whether the plotted minima (~0.05–0.06 m_e) are consistent with g′ = 4.

concerns.concern: At finite temperature, dμ/dn peaks can arise from thermally smeared jumps in μ. The temperature dependence in Fig. 3d therefore cannot be read as mass renormalization persisting to 77 K.
concerns.quote: The temperature dependence in Fig. 3d therefore cannot be read as mass renormalization surviving to 77 K.

concerns.concern: The probe bias dopes the sample by about half a moiré filling. It is unclear whether the fillings in Figs. 2–4 are equilibrium fillings or fillings under bias.
concerns.quote: V_b = 42 mV shifts the density by C_b·V_b/e ≈ 3.4×10¹¹ cm⁻² ≈ 0.5 n₀.

concerns.concern: The probe imposes a displacement field of about 0.2 V/nm, which could change layer polarization, flat-band dispersions and gaps. This is not quantified.
concerns.quote: This can change TBG layer polarization, flat-band dispersions and gaps.

concerns.concern: The sheared maps assume constant capacitances, ignoring the large filling-dependent quantum capacitance that enters through the probe capacitance.
concerns.quote: This ignores the large, filling-dependent quantum capacitance that enters through C_b.

concerns.concern: The SI-only quantum-capacitance correction shifts the ±4 peaks by about 0.2 in ν, the same order as the offsets central to the heavy/light reading. It is asserted to be negligible, risks circularity and is presumably temperature-dependent.
concerns.quote: That shift is the same order as the δ ≲ 0.1–0.2 offsets of the dμ/dn peaks from integer filling

concerns.concern: The atomic-limit model has two parameters (U₁, ε) tuned to match the data, so reproducing the two plateaus is partly by construction.
concerns.quote: Two free parameters fit two plateau temperatures and heights, so reproducing the plateaus is partly by construction.

concerns.concern: The entropy model uses zero f–c hybridization even though hybridization is tens of meV and is invoked to explain the masses over overlapping temperatures. This inconsistency is not explained.
concerns.quote: Why hybridization is negligible for entropy but essential for compressibility in overlapping temperature ranges is not explained.

concerns.concern: The model gives non-zero entropy as T → 0 and keeps rising without saturating at the combinatorial values. Low-temperature agreement is therefore not a stringent test.
concerns.quote: It also keeps rising without saturating at the combinatorial values, so low-T agreement is not a stringent test.

concerns.concern: A figure caption attributes the 4-fold plateau to strain-split flat bands, which is a band-splitting effect rather than an isospin local-moment degeneracy. The physical picture is unclear.
concerns.quote: That is a band-splitting effect, not obviously an isospin local-moment degeneracy, and the picture should be clarified.

concerns.concern: The heterostrain value used in the model is not constrained by independent observables.
concerns.quote: the heterostrain is not independently constrained.

concerns.concern: The large CNP entropy near 20 K (approaching ln 70) contradicts the reported ~10 meV CNP gap, which should give negligible thermally activated entropy.
concerns.quote: At least one of the gap, the entropy reference or the "random local moment" counting must be wrong.

concerns.concern: The entropy results are not quantitatively reconciled with prior SET measurements, which found ~1–2 k_B near ν = ±1 without plateaus.
concerns.quote: They should explain why their measurement reveals plateaus not seen there, or reconcile the discrepancy

concerns.concern: What is new relative to the existing STM, SET, entropy and thermoelectric literature is not clearly delineated.
concerns.quote: clearly delineate what is new relative to the STM, SET, entropy and thermoelectric literature.

concerns.concern: THF theory computed at 20 K is compared with 0.3 K and 4 K data and agrees only qualitatively. The predicted single symmetric peak does not match the measured sharp gap peak.
concerns.quote: The theory curve shows a single dμ/dν peak symmetric about ν = 2, whereas the measured feature is a sharp low-temperature gap peak.

concerns.concern: The absolute dμ/dn scale is not benchmarked against independent SET or compressibility data, so a systematic multiplicative error cannot be excluded.
concerns.quote: The absolute dμ/dn scale is not compared with independent SET or compressibility data, so a systematic multiplicative error cannot be excluded.

concerns.concern: The ~10 meV CNP gap is unusually large for non-aligned MATBG. hBN alignment, contamination by the phonon gap or the displacement field, and robustness to the integration constant and filling correction are not addressed.
concerns.quote: The CNP gap is much larger than typical values for non-aligned MATBG.

concerns.concern: The bandwidth and the CNP and ν = 2 gaps are not quantitatively compared with SET/capacitance results at similar angles. The gaps are also reported without uncertainties that include the relevant systematics.
concerns.quote: report gaps with uncertainties that include these systematics

concerns.concern: The stated gate capacitance implies a ~65 nm dielectric, contradicting the stated 30 nm top hBN. This undermines the absolute density and capacitance scales.
concerns.quote: implies a ~65 nm gate dielectric (ε ≈ 3.5). This contradicts the stated 30 nm top hBN

concerns.concern: The twist angle is quoted inconsistently in different places (1.06°, 1.07°, 1.08°, 1.1°).
concerns.quote: The angle is given as 1.06 ± 0.02° (text), 1.07° (Methods), 1.08° (Fig. 1b caption) and 1.1° (fabrication target).

concerns.concern: The Methods formula relating twist angle to moiré density is dimensionally inverted.
concerns.quote: The Methods expression θ = a(2/√3n₀)^{1/2} is dimensionally inverted.

concerns.concern: All data come from a single device and junction. No second device or junction confirms the entropy plateaus or the mass asymmetry.
concerns.quote: No second device, or second junction on the same device, confirms the entropy plateaus or the mass asymmetry.

concerns.concern: The ~1 µm² probe averages over twist-angle and strain disorder, and this inhomogeneity within the junction is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The ~1 µm² probe averages over twist-angle and strain disorder.

concerns.concern: The ν = 2 gap closes with an effective g ≈ 5.4. This is inconsistent with a spin-unpolarized intervalley-coherent singlet, where a bare spin flip gives g ≈ 2.
concerns.quote: A bare spin-flip excitation would give g ≈ 2.

concerns.concern: Two different ν = 2 gap values are given (1.3 meV from the μ jump and 1.75 meV from the linear fit).
concerns.quote: Δ = 1.3 meV from the μ jump differs from Δ₀ = 1.75 meV from the linear fit.

concerns.concern: The flat region of the ν = 2 gap versus field below ~1.5 T is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The flat region of Δ(B) below ~1.5 T is unexplained.

concerns.concern: The ν = 2 gap appears only at 0.3 K while the IKS comparison uses 20 K theory, and statements about the gap at '4 K' versus 'below 4 K' conflict.
concerns.quote: The gap appears only at 0.3 K, while the IKS comparison uses theory at 20 K.

concerns.concern: The persistence temperature of the mass asymmetry is stated variously as ~50, ~70 and ~77 K. The text also cites Fig. 3b for persistence to 50 K, but that figure has only 0.3 K and 4 K data.
concerns.quote: The text says Fig. 3b shows persistence to ~50 K, but Fig. 3b contains only 0.3 K and 4 K data.

concerns.concern: The 'factor of 10' mass renormalization is not supported by any plot of the mass ratio versus temperature with uncertainties.
concerns.quote: does not plot the mass ratio in a form, with uncertainties, that supports a "factor of 10" statement.

concerns.concern: The Landau-level spacing is called characteristic of massive Dirac fermions, but the formula used belongs to chiral parabolic, bilayer-graphene-like bands.
concerns.quote: The formula used, E_N − E₀ = ħω_c√(N(N−1)), belongs to chiral parabolic (bilayer-graphene-like) bands.

concerns.concern: The axis of the Landau-level fan figure is labelled inconsistently as √(N(N−1))B and √(N(N+1))B.
concerns.quote: Extended Fig. 2e is plotted versus √(N(N−1))B in one place and √(N(N+1))B in another.

concerns.concern: The field at which the zeroth-Landau-level degeneracy lifts is quoted inconsistently (>3.5 T versus >1.5 T).
concerns.quote: The zeroth-LL degeneracy lifting is quoted at >3.5 T (main text) and >1.5 T (Methods).

concerns.concern: The remote-band Landau-level fit has a non-zero intercept of about 60 mV that is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The remote-band fit has an undiscussed non-zero intercept of ~60 mV.

concerns.concern: The 0.174 m_e Landau-level mass at the CNP is not reconciled with the dμ/dn-derived mass values near ν = 0.
concerns.quote: The 0.174 m_e CNP mass is not reconciled with the Fig. 3a values near ν = 0.

concerns.concern: A Pomeranchuk-like non-monotonic dμ/dn feature near ν = 1 appears only in a figure and its caption, without discussion in the main text.
concerns.quote: appears only in the figure and its caption. It should be discussed in the main text or removed.

concerns.concern: The narrative of local moments 'emerging' on heating is directionally unclear, since the 8-fold moments become thermally accessible on heating rather than emerging.
concerns.quote: since 8-fold moments become thermally accessible on heating rather than "emerging".

concerns.concern: Phrases such as 'direct evidence' and 'experimental verification' overstate conclusions drawn from model-dependent derived quantities.
concerns.quote: Phrases such as "direct evidence" and "experimental verification" overstate model-dependent derived quantities.

concerns.concern: Essential methods (background determination, quantum-capacitance correction, zero-hybridization model) are relegated to the SI instead of the Methods.
concerns.quote: Essential methodological content is relegated to the SI

concerns.concern: The equation numbering in the Methods is wrong or confusing.
concerns.quote: Methods equation numbering ("solving equations (4) and (5)" refers to Eqs. (1) and (5); Eqs. 11–13 follow Eq. 7)

concerns.concern: Several figure references point to the wrong panels or figures.
concerns.quote: mismatched figure references (Fig. 3b/3d; Extended Fig. 3 versus 4 for the entropy extraction)

concerns.concern: The reference list contains duplicated entries.
concerns.quote: duplicated references (1/30, 23/57, 28/60)

concerns.concern: There are spelling errors in names and terms.
concerns.quote: "Wanatabe" for Watanabe and "Seeback" for Seebeck

concerns.concern: The claim that CNP entropy vanishes, as observed in SET measurements, is made without a citation.
concerns.quote: the uncited claim that CNP entropy vanishes "as observed in SET measurements of the inverse compressibility".
